title: Align auto-credit allocation rules and proration policy for mid-cycle enterprise contract changes
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Problem summary: Enterprise customers with reserved capacity, committed credits, or custom contract terms see incorrect credit allocations and prorated invoice lines when they change seat counts, capacity tiers, or add/remove premium features mid-billing-cycle. This causes accounting reconciliation churn, support escalations, and occasional negative/zero-dollar invoices that downstream systems mishandle.

Goal: Define a single canonical policy for (1) how auto-applied credits are allocated across overlapping charge windows, (2) proration math for capacity and seat changes, and (3) refund/credit issuance rules when adjustments create net negative charges. Produce product decisions, UI copy for invoices/console, billing-engine contract changes, and a migration plan for existing subscriptions. Also design a small pricing experiment to measure customer acceptance of pro-rata versus full-period billing on add-on purchases.

Scope: Enterprise contracts and dedicated customers only (hosted and dedicated); personal/self-serve seats are out-of-scope for this ticket and tracked separately.

Success metrics: 50% reduction in support tickets labeled "billing mismatch" for enterprise accounts in 30 days post-release; zero incidents where accounting closes month with unreconciled negative invoices; rollout documentation and training completed for CS/Finance.
acceptance_criteria: Billing engine applies credits deterministically: credit bucket ordering documented and implemented (reserved-capacity credits first, then promotional credits, then refund credits).
Proration math documented with examples for four scenarios: add seats mid-cycle, remove seats mid-cycle, upgrade capacity tier, downgrade capacity tier.
Invoice line items include a clear breakdown in Console and PDF: original charge, prorated adjustment, credit applied, net amount. UI copy approved by Legal.
When net charge < 0 after adjustments, system issues a one-time credit memo that can be applied to future invoices; negative invoice generation is prevented.
API /prorate endpoint and webhooks updated with new fields (proration_basis, credit_sources) and backward-compatible for existing integrators.
Integration tests cover edge cases: overlapping credit periods, exchange-rate rounding across currencies, and simultaneous multiple adjustments in same cycle.
Migration plan covers 12 months of historical subscriptions with a dry-run mode; Finance has a reconciliation report for first two billing cycles post-migration.

decisions: Adopt deterministic credit priority: reserved capacity commitments > contractual credits (e.g., pre-paid support) > promotional credits > refund/adjustment credits. This reduces ambiguity in ledger recognition.

Proration basis chosen: time-weighted on billing-cycle days (seconds-accurate) with mid-cycle effective timestamps; minimum billable unit is one minute for throughput seats; document exception rules for metered endpoints.

Net-negative outcome policy: never emit a negative invoice. Instead generate a credit memo that is applied to next invoice or available as a balance; exceptions require Finance approval for cash refund.
Rounding strategy: perform currency arithmetic in smallest unit (cents) and carry remainders to the most-recent invoice line to avoid cumulative rounding drift.
Experiment design: run 10% enterprise sample for 8 weeks comparing churn and support contacts; metric: conversion of add-on acceptance and support tickets per 100 customers.
